content.rendered:
Back in the River era, Bruce used to record his band’s rehearsal sessions so he could hear how they sounded as a unit and tweak his arrangements as required.

Since none of the recordings were meant to be kept for posterity, he didn’t use the best of equipment. In fact, he used a boom box situated so that it would capture the band’s full sound.

None of the singers (including Bruce himself) were miked, which means that any vocals were almost always inaudible in the recordings. Combined with Bruce’s penchant for bluffing lyrics during these sessions, trying to decipher what he’s singing in these tapes is a futile exercise.

Occasionally, though, one of the band members would stand close enough to the boom box to be clearly picked up, and that’s hilariously the case with today’s entry. See if you can guess who it was:

We likely wouldn’t even know the title of this abandoned song had The Big Man not been standing so close to the recorder, but we can’t possibly miss him or his shouted “I Don’t Wanna Be!” vocals.

As far as we know, “I Don’t Wanna Be” never developed into a full song. It’s melody, however, is very familiar. After at least a half dozen failed melodic attempts, Bruce grafted an evolved version of “I Don’t Wanna Be” onto “Jackson Cage.”

I Don’t Wanna Be
Recorded: May 1979 (rehearsal only)
Never released
Never performed

© September 26, 2021

excerpt.rendered: This melodic ancestor to “Jackson Cage” captures The Big Man standing just a bit too close to the mic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Wanna Be With You
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A lost power-pop classic, "I Wanna Be With You" charms with its lovesick loser protagonist, fiercely defiant lyrics and exuberant arrangement.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Under the Gun
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Under the Gun" donated its lyrics to "The River" and "Wreck on the Highway" but there's still a terrific rocker hiding away in the vault somewhere. Let's trace its evolution to get a sense of what the final song might promise.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Slow Fade
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Still missing in action after all these years: whatever happened to the smoking E Street Band song known only as "Slow Fade" from bootleg rehearsal tapes? Take a listen to this remarkable track inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Wanna Start a New Life
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This gorgeous Jackson Browne-ian work-in-progress ballad might have made for a gorgeous song had Bruce completed it.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Wanna Marry You
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This early love song hasn't aged well but it paved the way for Bruce's more mature and nuanced reflections on love and marriage.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Find It Where You Can
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Missing in action: this early lyrical forerunner to "Tougher Than the Rest" made it all the way to an E Street Band rehearsal but never to the studio.
